recentItems.title: Gang leader found guilty of Tupac murder | DW News
recentItems.description:
A Las Vegas jury has convicted Duane “Keffe D” Davis of first‑degree murder over the 1996 killing of hip-hop star Tupac Shakur.  The court heard Davis, a former Los Angeles gang leader, had targeted Shakur for beating up his nephew. He faces a sentence of life in prison, but says he will appeal. The previously unsolved murder has captivated hip-hop fans for decades. #dwnews

recentItems.title: Flash flood tears through Grand Canyon | DW News
recentItems.description:
The Grand Canyon is considered one of the wonders of the natural world. Last Saturday a major flash flood tore through part of the canyon in the US state of Arizona. At least two people were killed, while several others remain missing. Dozens of visitors had to be evacuated by helicopter. The Grand Canyon attracts millions of visitors every year. So how did one of the world's most famous natural wonders turn into a deadly flood zone? We spoke with Grand Canyon researcher and expert Tom Martin, and with meteorologist Robert Rickey.

recentItems.title: Kurdish-led SDF has dissolved under a deal which recognizes Kurdish rights | DW News
recentItems.description:
The Kurdish Syrian Democratic Forces, which for years operated largely outside the control of Damascus, are being absorbed into the Syrian state. It's a major breakthrough for President Ahmed al-Sharaa, but one that leaves big questions over Kurdish rights and Syria's long-term stability. We spoke to Kristian Brakel, political analyst and director of the Heinrich Böll Foundation's Beirut office.

recentItems.title: Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant on emergency power as diesel runs low | DW News
recentItems.description:
Europe's largest nuclear power plant has been running without external electricity for more than a week.  The Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia plant is relying on emergency diesel generators to keep its six shut-down reactors cool. Nuclear safety expert Dr Nikolaus Müllner tells DW how catastrophic the consequences could be if the diesel runs out.
